top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities with magnitude and direction using vectors.
Add vectors graphically and interpret the resultant vector.
Resolve vectors into horizontal and vertical components using right-triangle relationships.
Explain the independence of horizontal and vertical motion in ideal projectile motion.
Predict how launch speed and angle affect trajectory, range, maximum height, and time of flight.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce vectors as objects with both magnitude and direction, distinct from scalars.
key_visuals: A floor grid with coordinate axes
Several colored arrows of different lengths and directions
Labels showing magnitude, direction angle, and units
student_actions: Select arrows and read their magnitudes and directions.
Compare a scalar quantity, such as mass, with a vector quantity, such as displacement or velocity.
Rotate and resize a vector arrow to see how direction and magnitude change independently.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how two displacement vectors combine to form a resultant vector.
key_visuals: Two movable vectors on a grid
A ghosted copy of the second vector placed at the tip of the first
A resultant arrow from the starting point to the final tip
A numerical readout of resultant magnitude and angle
student_actions: Drag vectors into tip-to-tail arrangement.
Toggle the resultant vector on and off.
Compare the resultant with the original vectors and describe what it represents.

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect a vector to its x- and y-components and the trigonometric relationships among them.
key_visuals: A single angled vector projected onto horizontal and vertical axes
Dashed component arrows forming a right triangle
Angle marker from the positive x-axis
Equations such as Ax = A cos θ and Ay = A sin θ
student_actions: Adjust the vector angle and magnitude.
Observe how the x- and y-components change.
Use component values to reconstruct the original vector magnitude and direction.

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector components to the initial velocity of a projectile.
key_visuals: A launcher aimed at an adjustable angle
An initial velocity arrow split into horizontal and vertical component arrows
Numeric displays for launch speed, angle, vx0, and vy0
student_actions: Set a launch speed and angle.
Predict whether the horizontal or vertical component will be larger.
Check the component values and relate them to the launch angle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate that horizontal velocity remains constant while vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
key_visuals: A projectile moving along a parabolic path
Velocity vectors shown at several points along the flight
Separate side panels showing horizontal motion at constant spacing and vertical motion with changing spacing
A downward acceleration vector labeled g
student_actions: Step through the projectile motion frame by frame.
Compare the horizontal velocity arrows at different times.
Observe the vertical velocity shrinking, reaching zero at the top, then growing downward.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show that the projectile trajectory emerges from combining uniform horizontal motion with accelerated vertical motion.
key_visuals: A time-stamped grid of projectile positions
Horizontal and vertical component motion traces
A combined parabolic trajectory overlay
Synchronized markers for x-position and y-position over time
student_actions: Run the horizontal-only, vertical-only, and combined motions.
Identify how each component contributes to the final position.
Explain why the combined path is curved rather than straight.

scenes.brief_purpose: Let students explore how launch speed and angle change range, maximum height, and time of flight.
key_visuals: Interactive sliders for initial speed and launch angle
Multiple trajectory arcs with different colors
Markers for range and maximum height
Summary table comparing trials
student_actions: Perform several launches with different speeds and angles.
Record how range and height change.
Compare complementary launch angles and note similarities or differences in range under ideal conditions.
